title: Finished Cooking; I Have Come
paragraphs: He had invited friends to a feast. Two of the friends arrived even before midnoon. His wife feigned anger, “What dear! You have invited your friends without intimating to me in advance.”
“I bought murrel fish. I would be only too happy to share them with my friends. Since you would also like the gesture, I invited those two friends. Hurry up! Look after the cooking.”

The mistress of the house was activated immediately. She cleaned the rice, put it in boiling water, lighted the stove, chopped the fish into equal pieces, and after mixing the requisite amount of spice, salt, and tamarind, put them one after another into the boiling curry. She kept herself focused upon the food being prepared on both the stoves.
It is indeed a joyful thing for her to serve food to the guests and sit eating with them.
The husband, seated on the veranda of the house, repeatedly asked his wife, “Is the food ready? Why is it taking so long? Why is it taking so long?”
She didn’t relish his loud reminders.
> The anicham flower withers away when smelt; > The guests would turn sullen when looked at with a frown.

kept ringing as a caution in her heart. Just as she was rushing through with cooking, she heard her husband’s harsh query, “At what time would you finish cooking? At what time would it be served? At what time would we be eating it?”

The lady wearing a smile on her face placed the plantain leaves on the floor and said, “Let me state the present time and future time in past tense -- here, I finished cooking. I am right here for serving. You three could come and start eating.” One of the friends was all praise for her:
“Looks the mistress of the house has a sound mastery over grammar also, as she reigns like a queen!”
“Well, I am no queen - I am an ordinary woman discharging my household duties and of course with some knowledge of literature. That is all.”
Her proud and loving husband enquired, “Isn’t this Tolkāppiyam? You can as well recite the entire verse.”
“Let the feast be over, then recitation can follow.”
After finishing the feast, she didn’t forget to serve the delicacy of Tolkāppiyam:
> To attribute the action of a verb to the past > While it bears on the present and future > Is to suggest exigency, > So do the literate hold. > > (Collatikāram : Viṉaiyiyal, verse 44)
Note: An event that links the present and the future times can be expressed in the form of past tense.
